question: Can a separately compiled Rust integration-test executable receive the producer's exact canonical request bytes when it independently rebuilds the same named source, while refusing a renamed module and a changed request profile?
route: one producer integration-test target plus one independently pinned consumer integration-test target

types_and_domains.request_bytes: canonical UTF-8 JSON emitted by the producer target
excluded: noncommutative algebra beyond retained ordered diagrams and histories

quantifiers: For the one frozen request, one producer process writes bytes; three separately compiled consumer-target process invocations each read those bytes and independently rebuild the case-selected current source artifacts.

candidate_grammar.accepted: same module name, source body, arithmetic value, external leaf, profile and imported source/residual snapshots

controls.changed-profile: change only the first profile occurrence from v0 to v1 in consumer memory

evaluation.renamed-module: Refused: serialized source or residual snapshot mismatch
evaluation.source_coordinate_check: both staged files must match the two frozen SHA-256 digests
evaluation.regression_check: unchanged-lock Clippy and selected native Rust tests must pass

budgets.semantic_process_deadline: not separately installed; all four invocations are bounded by the 15-minute workflow job limit
budgets.memory_limit: not installed; peak RSS must be reported missing unless the runner measures it

refusal_and_residual_policy: A wrong outcome in any case is a replayable failure, not Unknown.
A build, source-digest or dependency failure is InvalidContext and cannot support a semantic claim.
Timeout or unmeasured completion preserves Unknown for the affected case.

Success remains a finite same-repository, same-toolchain experiment; it does not establish an independent implementation, Research 0090 coverage, Research 0092 promotion, M6 closure, native free, arithmetic-universality or hypothesized-arithmetic-truth.
